blogs.title: The Great Mimicker: When Leiomyomas Masquerade as Adnexal Masses in Pregnancy
blogs.description: This post will explore the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing cystic degenerating leiomyomas from ovarian pathology during pregnancy. We'll discuss how the 'steric bulk' of the gravid uterus limits imaging windows, why pedunculated myomas can simulate adnexal cysts, and the added value of MRI for determining the relationship between masses and the uterine wall. A critical look at why even comprehensive imaging can get it wrong—and what that means for preoperative counseling.

blogs.title: CA-125 in Pregnancy: Navigating the False Positives and False Reassurance
blogs.description: An evidence-based dive into the physiology of CA-125 during pregnancy, which peaks in the first and third trimesters but can be elevated in numerous benign conditions including leiomyomas, endometriosis, and even normal pregnancy. We'll discuss why isolated measurements are nearly useless, how serial trending can be more informative, and the dangers of over-relying on tumor markers when malignancy is on the differential for a pregnant patient.

blogs.title: Cutting During Pregnancy: When Surgery Beats Expectant Management for Abdominal Masses
blogs.description: This post will tackle the clinical decision-making framework for operating on large abdominal masses during pregnancy. We'll analyze the key indications that pushed this case toward surgery—worsening symptoms, mass size, risk of torsion/rupture, and restriction of uterine growth—against the backdrop of conservative management. A discussion of optimal timing (second trimester) and how to balance maternal safety with fetal preservation.

blogs.title: Myomectomy in Pregnancy: Technical Pearls and Perioperative Prophylaxis
blogs.description: A practical guide to performing safe myomectomy during pregnancy, including why pedunculated myomas are the most amenable to resection, the role of intraoperative fetal heart rate monitoring, and the evidence behind progesterone prophylaxis for tocolysis. We'll also cover approach selection (laparotomy vs. laparoscopy) based on mass characteristics and gestational age, and postoperative considerations including blood transfusion and infection management.

blogs.title: Delivery Dilemmas: Planning Childbirth Around Residual Pelvic Masses
blogs.description: An obstetric-focused post examining how the location and size of residual myomas should influence delivery planning. We'll discuss why a posterior isthmic myoma can obstruct labor, the timing of elective cesarean delivery after second-trimester myomectomy, strategies to minimize uterine scar rupture risk, and the natural history of myoma regression postpartum that may allow for expectant management of residual disease.
